title: The Day the Page Woke Up
skyStory: Welcome, you two. The moon is brand new tonight, only two percent lit, curled up in Sagittarius like a cat pretending to be asleep. It has been waiting for this page to open since October and is trying very hard to look casual. Mars brought streamers. Saturn brought a clipboard. A November gale rattles the shutters, which is the sky's version of a drumroll.

reading: First day of a brand-new reading, and the Tiger has already opened four tabs about it. Lovely. Close three. A new moon is a seed, not a forest, and the [[Knight of Wands]] would like you to plant exactly one thing today and then walk away whistling.

Around 11:40 am somebody will thank you for something you forgot you did. Do not wave it off. Do not say it was nothing. Say thank you back, out loud, with your whole face, and let it land like snow on a mitten. Life Path 3 means words are your fire. Today, practise catching them as well as throwing them. Ten points to the Tiger for every compliment received without a rebuttal.
joel.mission: Write one sentence about what you hope this month brings, fold it into a tiny square, and tuck it somewhere you will forget.
joel.omen: A chimney puffing smoke in a perfectly straight line. The cabin approves of new beginnings and says keep going.
joel.stoneWhy: Nancy's stone, for a first page

reading: Hello, Mountain. The sky has been rehearsing its welcome speech for you all week and still fumbled the opening line. It is fine. You have told enough stories to know the good part always comes in the middle, after the hands start moving.

A new moon in Sagittarius wants to know where you are headed, and you are allowed to answer: somewhere with a good view and a warm drink. The Wood Rat in you has already noticed something small that nobody else has, maybe a crooked picture frame or a word misspelled on a sign. Keep it to yourself until 4 pm, then tell it as the best story of the day.
nancy.mission: Turn the ruby on your pinky to face outward for one whole conversation, like a tiny lighthouse beam.
nancy.omen: A gull standing on one leg on something it definitely should not be standing on. Bold choices are in season.
nancy.stoneWhy: the Fire is watching over you

together.text: Send each other one word that sums up how this month should feel, without conferring. Compare them at bedtime. If they match, the cabin chimney puffs twice. If they do not, combine them into one ridiculous new word and use it all week.

title: The Day of the Runaway Toque
skyStory: A sliver of moon, five percent and grinning, is still loitering in Sagittarius with its boots on the dashboard. It wants adventure. It is November, so adventure means wind strong enough to steal a hat off a stranger and hand it to someone three streets over. Jupiter, the landlord of Sagittarius, is laughing too loudly at its own jokes again.

reading: The cabin has a draft, and the draft has opinions. Something you set down this morning will not be where you left it by noon. It has not been taken. It has wandered, the way a toque wanders in a gale, and it will come back when it gets bored.

Meanwhile, a small fire is asking to be built properly: kindling first, patience second, big logs last. That is your afternoon. One task, laid in order, lit once. The [[Knight of Pentacles]] is the slow horse in the deck and today it outruns everyone. Around 2:20 pm you will want to start a second thing. Put a log on the first one instead.
joel.mission: Find the oldest pen in the house and use it for every note today, out of respect for its long service.
joel.omen: A hat tumbling down the street on its own. Something you let go of is having a lovely time without you.
joel.stoneWhy: carry the spark in your pocket
joel.elementWhy: the gale is in charge today

reading: Sagittarius keeps throwing ideas at you like a kid tossing snowballs at a window. Most of them miss. One of them, around mid-morning, lands perfectly and makes a satisfying thunk. That is the one. You will know it because your hands start drawing it in the air before your mouth catches up.

The gift of the Rat today is spotting the shortcut nobody else sees: the side door, the faster queue, the button on the bottom row. Use it once, gleefully, then show one other person where it is. Helping someone level up is your favourite trick, and today it costs you exactly nine seconds.
nancy.mission: Teach somebody one tiny trick you know, like folding a fitted sheet or a keyboard shortcut, and accept the applause.
nancy.omen: A gutter dripping onto exactly the same spot all day. Small steady effort is wearing a path through something big.

together.text: Each of you choose a stranger's hat today and give it a secret name, like Captain Woolsworth or The Grand Pompom. Report back with the best one. The winner gets bragging rights until Friday and must use a pompous voice when claiming them.

title: The Day of the Kettle Conspiracy
skyStory: Ten percent of the moon is showing, which is the lunar equivalent of peeking through the blinds. Sagittarius is packing its bags for tomorrow's move and keeps finding things it forgot it owned: a compass, three arrows, a half-written postcard to Saturn. The kettle in every kitchen is in on this somehow. Nobody will say how.

reading: Your brain will hand you eleven brilliant ideas before breakfast. The Tiger loves a buffet. But a very serious knight is standing in the doorway with its arms crossed, and it only lets one idea through. Pick the one that makes you laugh, not the one that makes you busy.

Somewhere around 1:05 pm a kettle, a microwave or a dryer will beep at you three times. Each beep is a question. First: is this the main thing? Second: have you looked out a window today? Third: have you told anyone that they did a good job? Answer all three before the next beep, or the appliances win.
joel.mission: Make a list of ten ideas, then cross out nine with great ceremony, saying 'not today, friend' to each one.
joel.omen: Steam fogging a window in the shape of a lopsided heart. Someone is thinking about you warmly.
joel.elementWhy: aim it, do not spray it

reading: The shore is quiet today and so are you, in the good way, the way a cat is quiet right before it does something magnificent. People will expect you to talk first. Let the silence stretch one extra beat. Somebody will rush to fill it and reveal exactly what you needed to know.

The [[Six of Swords]] has its little boat out today, and the water is calm for once. Whatever you have been carrying across, set one small piece of it down in the hull and let the boat do some of the work. You do not have to row and steer and carry all at once. Joel is on the far bank, waving his arms too much.
nancy.mission: Leave the room one minute early from something today and spend that minute looking at the horizon or the nearest tree.
nancy.omen: A boat, a canoe or even a picture of one. The crossing is going better than you think.
nancy.stoneWhy: layer by layer, like the tide
nancy.elementWhy: a light breeze in the sails

together.text: Pick one thing each that you will absolutely finish by Friday. Say it to the other person in one sentence, no hedging allowed. Then check in Friday night with a single word: done, nearly or sneakily rebranded. All three are acceptable answers, but only one gets a cheer.

title: The Moon Moves Into Nancy's Spare Room
skyStory: Big news on the mountain. The moon, seventeen percent lit and carrying far too many boxes, has moved into Capricorn, Nancy's sign. Saturn is giving it the tour: here is the good chair, here is the window with the view, please use a coaster. The moon has never been this tidy in its life. It is also Friday the thirteenth, which Saturn finds frankly beneath it.

reading: With the moon off visiting Nancy's side of the map, your job today is caretaker. Keep the cabin fire going, keep the kettle full, keep the jokes coming. Somebody near you is having a heavier day than they let on. You will notice it by the way they hold their mug with both hands.

Offer one small kindness without announcing it. Then, and this is the hard part, let someone do one small kindness for you without immediately trying to repay it. If someone holds a door, walk through it. Do not race ahead to hold the next door. The universe is keeping score, and today it only counts the doors you walk through.
joel.mission: Switch the onyx to your right wrist at lunchtime and send the mountain one silent cheer for her big moon day.
joel.omen: A black cat crossing your path from left to right. Excellent luck, actually. The cat insists, and it has paperwork.
joel.stoneWhy: clear light for a clear head
joel.elementWhy: grounded so the mountain can shine

reading: The moon is staying in your guest room for two days and it brought a housewarming gift: everything you touch today goes a little more smoothly than it should. Doors open before you push. The printer behaves. A sentence you have been chewing on for a week finally comes out exactly right.

Saturn, your ruler, is in its cozy-sweater era and wants you to enjoy this instead of auditing it. The [[Knight of Pentacles]] is not asking you to earn this one. Accept the easy day. Life Path 11 knows a gift when it sees one; the trick is unwrapping it without reading the instructions first.
nancy.mission: Sit in the best seat of any room you enter today, as if the moon is paying your rent.
nancy.omen: A perfectly stacked pile of something, firewood or books or plates. The mountain is pleased with your work.
nancy.stoneWhy: earth stone for the earth sign

together.text: Tonight, each name one place that feels like home that is not a house. A certain bench, a bend in the road, a smell. Trade them. The moon, newly moved in and slightly homesick itself, will be eavesdropping and taking notes for its own housewarming.

title: The Day of the Two Blue Mittens
skyStory: Second night of the moon in Capricorn, twenty-four percent lit, and it has rearranged Saturn's furniture without asking. Saturn is quietly furious and quietly impressed. Something in the air today is doubled: echoes on the shore, two crows where one should be, reflections that arrive slightly early. Watch for pairs. The sky is in a matching mood and it will not be subtle.

reading: Somewhere today, on a fence post, a railing or a car antenna, you will see a single blue mitten that someone has rescued and perched there for its owner. Take a picture. Do not ask questions. The mitten knows what it is doing.

Here is the twist: Nancy is going to see one too, a different mitten, same shade of blue, same perching posture, and you will both send the picture within the same ten minutes. Don't even scream. The [[Wheel of Fortune]] is simply showing off. Fire Tiger and Wood Rat, two lost-and-found mittens, one sky with a ridiculous sense of humour. Frame it in your mind.
joel.mission: Put one lost thing back where its owner will find it, and perch it at eye level with dignity.
joel.omen: Two crows on one roof, facing opposite directions. You and Nancy are covering the whole sky between you.
joel.elementWhy: two halves of a matching pair

reading: The moon is in your sign one last night and it wants to leave you a parting gift. It is small, slightly damp and blue. You will spot it before anyone else does, because the Wood Rat always spots it first.

When your phone buzzes with Joel's mitten picture, a minute or two after you sent yours, do the full reaction: gasp, hands up, maybe a small spin. This is a ΔΕΣ moment of the highest order and it deserves your best storytelling hands. Afterwards, write down the exact time. [[The Star]] likes a written record, and you will want proof when you tell this story at a party in three years.
nancy.mission: Tell the mitten story to one person today, with full hand choreography, and do not trim it for time.
nancy.omen: A child's lost toy waiting politely on a windowsill. Someone is taking care of small things, and it is noticed.

together.text: Compare mitten photos and decide which one is the braver mitten. Then invent a tiny backstory: where it came from, who lost it, what adventure it is on. Keep the story going all week. By Friday the mittens should have names, rivals and at least one dramatic rescue.

title: The Day of the Ridiculous Invention
skyStory: The moon has bounced into Aquarius, a third lit and buzzing with gadgets. Aquarius moons are the mad scientists of the zodiac: wild hair, a lab coat with pockets full of springs, ideas nobody asked for. First quarter means a little push. Today, the push is sideways, and it comes with blueprints drawn on a napkin.

reading: Your brain has been waiting for an Aquarius moon all month. Something annoying at home or at work will suddenly reveal its fix to you, and the fix will be both brilliant and slightly absurd, like using a clothes peg as a cable organiser or a muffin tin as a desk tray.

Build it. Do not improve it, do not plan version two, do not start a spreadsheet of related fixes. The [[Knight of Wands]] says one invention, and the Tiger should be extremely proud of exactly one invention. Around 4:30 pm, show it to someone like it is a museum piece. Accept their compliments without explaining how it could be better.
joel.mission: Rename one ordinary object in the house with a grand inventor's name and use only that name until bedtime.
joel.omen: A string of lights with exactly one bulb out. Perfection is overrated; the rest are shining fine.

reading: The Rat is an inventor by nature, the clever one who notices the latch that does not quite catch. Today you will fix something in about four seconds that has bothered someone else for months. They will look at you like you performed a magic trick.

Let them. Do not say it was easy. Say 'yes, I am remarkable', or at least think it very loudly. Aquarius loves a genius who does not apologise. In the evening, tell the story of the fix with full hand gestures, including a dramatic pause right before the click. The pause is the whole performance.
nancy.mission: Draw a terrible blueprint for a machine that does one silly chore, like sorting socks by mood, and label every part.
nancy.omen: A squirrel outwitting a bird feeder. Clever creatures always find a way, and today you are one of them.

together.text: Invent a ridiculous gadget together over messages. Joel names it, Nancy names its secret feature, Joel adds a warning label, Nancy writes the slogan. Stop after four rounds. Saturn will pretend not to read it and secretly want one.

title: The Day the Wind Took Attendance
skyStory: Forty-two percent of the moon is lit and it is holding onto Aquarius with both hands, because a proper November gale is barrelling in off the Atlantic. Aquarius is an air sign that rarely gets to show off like this. It is taking attendance: every loose leaf, every flapping bin lid, every brave umbrella. Everyone is accounted for. Several are now in a different town.

reading: The wind will rattle the cabin windows today and you will feel the urge to brace against everything at once. Don't. Cabins have stood through worse gales than this one by doing one thing: staying put and keeping the fire lit. Pick the thing that matters most and stand behind it.

Someone will come to you with a problem shaped like a tangled kite string. You will want to grab it and untangle the whole thing yourself, in public, at speed. Instead, hold one end and let them work the knots. Life Path 3 is the teacher, and the best teachers know when to hand the string back.
joel.mission: Step outside for one full minute in the wind, arms out like a kite, and shout one thing you are proud of.
joel.omen: A bin lid cartwheeling down the road. Chaos is happening, but none of it is yours to chase.
joel.stoneWhy: anchor stone for a windy day

reading: Gale day on the shore. The waves are showing off, throwing spray over the rocks like confetti at a very dramatic wedding. You are the rock, of course. Steady, unbothered, faintly amused, getting a little wet and not minding.

Courage today looks quiet. It looks like saying the one honest sentence in a meeting that everyone else is thinking. It looks like asking the question you assumed was obvious. The [[Strength]] card is not a lion-wrestler today; it is a hand resting gently on a lion's head while the wind howls. That is you. Hand gestures optional, but encouraged.
nancy.mission: Say the honest sentence before 3 pm, then reward yourself with something warm in a mug.
nancy.omen: A gull hovering perfectly still in a gale, going nowhere on purpose. Holding your position is progress.
nancy.stoneWhy: sea stone for a sea storm
nancy.elementWhy: the waves are on your side

together.text: Each of you tell the other one brave thing you did today, no matter how small. Answering an email you were dodging counts. Wearing the bright scarf counts. The wind is taking attendance, and it marks you both present with a gold star.

title: The Day of the Perfect Half
skyStory: Exactly half the moon is lit tonight, and Aquarius is very smug about the symmetry. Half light, half dark, perfectly balanced, like a cookie split fairly between two friends who have been negotiating since lunch. The gale has calmed to a grumble. Saturn says balance is earned. The moon says balance is a mood. They agree to disagree, politely.

reading: The [[Six of Pentacles]] has the scales out today, and it is weighing one thing only: how much you give versus how much you let in. Spoiler: the scale is tipped so far toward giving that it has fallen off the table. The moon would like a word.

Today's task is lopsided on purpose. Someone will offer to help with something you could easily do alone. Say yes. Say yes even if they do it slower, differently, or with a worse playlist. Watch the scale wobble back toward the middle. Half moon, half day, half the work. The Tiger is allowed to nap in a sunbeam for exactly one half hour.
joel.mission: Accept the next offer of help you receive, however tiny, and say only 'thank you, that would be great'.
joel.omen: A shoelace coming undone exactly halfway through a walk. Pause, retie, and notice that pausing was the point.

reading: The half moon is a seesaw and you are, as usual, the person who quietly makes sure everyone gets a turn. Today the seesaw wants you to sit on it yourself. Something you have been putting second, a hobby or a nap or a book, gets moved to the front of the line.

Patience is your superpower, but it has a twin called postponement, and the two of them dress alike. At around 7:15 tonight, check which one is driving. If it is postponement, kindly ask it to move to the back seat and start the thing you love for twenty minutes. Saturn will hold your calls.
nancy.mission: Spend twenty minutes on something purely for fun, and refuse to call it productive.
nancy.omen: A seesaw or a balance scale in an unexpected place. Things are evening out in your favour.
nancy.stoneWhy: Joel's fire, for your own joy

together.text: Split something fairly today: the last biscuit, the good pen, the window seat. Do it with ridiculous ceremony, as if a peace treaty is being signed. Then each report who won the negotiation. Both of you will claim victory. Both of you will be right.

title: The Day of the Fog Letters
skyStory: The moon has drifted into Pisces, sixty-two percent lit and dreamy, and it brought the fog with it. Pisces moons blur edges: the end of the wharf, the top of the hill, the line between a daydream and a plan. Sound carries strangely. A foghorn somewhere is trying to say something meaningful and keeps losing its place.

reading: Fog sits around the cabin like a wool blanket and muffles everything, including, for once, your to-do list. You will not be able to see the whole day from the porch. Good. Do the next visible thing, then the next, and let the rest stay in the mist where it belongs.

Today you are the oar. Somebody close to you is mid-crossing, and the help they need is not advice. It is steady rowing: showing up, the same time, the same warmth, no speeches. Life Path 3 will itch to give a talk. Hand over a warm mug instead. Rowing quietly is the loudest thing you can do.
joel.mission: Send Nancy a picture of something blurry and beautiful, without any explanation at all.
joel.omen: A porch light glowing through fog. You are visible to the people who need you, even when you feel hidden.

reading: Fog on the water, and the [[Six of Swords]] is pushing off from the shore again. The crossing is not finished, but today you can see a little further than last week. A shape on the far side is starting to look familiar, like a cabin with its chimney smoking.

You do not have to row hard today. Pisces wants you to drift a little, trust the current, and notice what floats by. Around 10:20 am an old memory will surface, something funny you had forgotten. Tell it to someone. Stories are how you steer through fog. Joel, on the far bank, is holding up a lantern too, very badly, slightly upside down.
nancy.mission: Write a two-line note to future-you, seal it in an envelope, and date it for the solstice.
nancy.omen: A foghorn or a distant train, sounding exactly twice. Someone on the far shore is calling your name, kindly.

together.text: Tonight, each of you light something small, a candle or a lamp, and put it in a window that faces the other's direction. Text a photo. Two little lights across the fog, showing each other the way home. The foghorn approves, at length.

title: The Day of the Unsent Postcard
skyStory: Seventy-one percent lit and growing, the moon is still swimming in Pisces, doing lazy backstrokes and humming. Waxing gibbous moons are almost there and know it. Neptune, ruler of Pisces, has left a stack of blank postcards on every windowsill. Nobody knows where the stamps are. That is part of the charm, and also extremely Neptune.

reading: The Tiger is tired and too proud to say so. Pisces sees through that in a heartbeat. Today, rest counts as work. A walk counts. Staring at the woodstove counts. If anyone asks what you accomplished, say 'I recharged the fire' and leave it there, mysteriously.

Late afternoon, around 4:44, you will think of a sentence that would make someone's whole week. Write it down. Maybe send it, maybe keep it for later. The [[Four of Cups]] is offering a gift you have been too busy to notice, and today the gift is your own quiet. Take it with both paws.
joel.mission: Write a postcard to someone you admire, address it, and keep it in a book as a bookmark until you are ready.
joel.omen: A cat asleep in a window, completely unbothered by the world. That is the assignment.

reading: The Rat is curled in the nest today with one eye open, and the open eye is noticing everything: who needs a laugh, which plant needs water, what the cat is plotting. You will get three small chances to help someone level up before lunch.

Take one. Leave the other two. Pisces wants you to save some energy for yourself and stop running the whole tide single-handed. In the evening, write a postcard you will never send, addressed to the mountain you used to be, telling her how far you have come. Read it out loud once, dramatically, to an empty room.
nancy.mission: Water one plant, or one person, with a compliment so specific it makes them blink.
nancy.omen: A bird bathing in a puddle with total commitment. Joy does not need a reason or an audience.

together.text: No missions tonight. Each of you pick one cozy thing, a blanket, a book, a long shower with music, and do it without guilt. Send one emoji to report in. The moon is filling up slowly, and so are you, one quiet evening at a time.

title: The Moon Knocks on the Tiger's Door
skyStory: The moon has charged into Aries, Joel's own sign, eighty percent lit and already wearing a cape. Mars, the ruler of Aries, has rolled out the red carpet, then set it slightly on fire for dramatic effect. Everything feels faster. Kettles boil sooner. The Tiger's ears are up and twitching. Even the November drizzle seems to be running late for something.

reading: Your sign, your moon, your home field. Today you can feel the crowd cheering, and the crowd is mostly made of your own good ideas chanting your name. Lovely. Now listen carefully to the [[Knight of Wands]]: aim. One target. A Tiger that pounces on everything catches nothing but air.

Choose the project that has been waiting the longest and give it one burst of glorious Aries energy before 2 pm. Not a plan, an actual push. After that, step away and let someone tell you it looks great. If you feel the urge to start something new around 5 pm, write it on a sticky note and stick it to tomorrow.
joel.mission: Wear something red, a sock counts, and roar quietly at your reflection once before leaving the house.
joel.omen: A red car pulling out of a spot exactly as you arrive. The way is clearing; take it.
joel.stoneWhy: your own stone, home for a visit

reading: The moon has gone to visit Joel's side of the map and the Fire is going to be extra loud today. You may receive a burst of messages with too many exclamation marks. This is weather. Enjoy it like a bonfire on the beach: warm, a bit wild, best enjoyed from a comfortable distance.

Borrow some of that Aries spark for yourself. One thing you have been patiently waiting on deserves a nudge today, not a polite nudge, a cheerful shove. Saturn says patience is noble. Mars says patience has had its turn. You get to decide, and the ruby on your pinky is quietly voting for Mars.
nancy.mission: Send one message today that starts with 'Right, let's do this' and actually mean it.
nancy.omen: A fireplace glowing through a stranger's window. The Fire is thinking of you from somewhere warm.
nancy.stoneWhy: carrying his fire on his day

together.text: Joel sends Nancy one bold idea in exactly seven words. Nancy replies with one bold idea in exactly eleven, for her Life Path. No explaining allowed. Then each picks the idea they like best from the other and takes one tiny step toward it before bed.

title: The Day of Three-Eleven
skyStory: Second day of the moon in Aries, eighty-eight percent lit and impatient for the full thing. Mars is pacing. The sky is doing arithmetic in the margins: three and eleven, Joel's Life Path beside Nancy's. Numbers will be suspiciously loud today. Clocks, house numbers, page numbers, all of them nudging each other and whispering. Somebody up there has a calculator and a sense of mischief.

reading: At exactly 3:11 this afternoon you will glance at a clock for no reason. Your Life Path beside hers, side by side on the screen like two friends on a porch. Smile at it. That is the polite thing to do with a number that has clearly been waiting for you.

At 3:12, your phone will buzz. It is Nancy, and she has sent a photo of the same time, from her own clock, without a word. DES. The [[Wheel of Fortune]] has gone fully theatrical. Reply with only a picture of the onyx bracelet, switched to your right wrist. No caption needed. Some coincidences deserve silence and a very big grin.
joel.mission: Count to eleven in three different voices before your first coffee, just to warm up the numbers.
joel.omen: A house number with a three and a one in it. You are on the right street, in every sense.
joel.stoneWhy: her stone, sending strength her way

reading: The Wood Rat sees patterns other people miss, and today the pattern practically waves at you. The number eleven will turn up three times before lunch: a page number, a bus, a queue ticket. You will notice every single one and start keeping count on your fingers.

When the clock flips to 3:11, take the picture. Send it before you can talk yourself out of it. What happens next is a full don't even scream situation, and you will be grinning at your phone like it told you a secret. Then do the hand gesture. You know the one. The big one, with both hands and a little flourish at the end.
nancy.mission: Keep a tally of every eleven you spot today and announce the final score at dinner, with a drumroll.
nancy.omen: Three birds landing on a wire, one after the other. Two friends, one sky, perfect timing.

together.text: Save the 3:11 photos side by side somewhere you will both find them again. Give the coincidence an official name, like The Great Clock Incident, and agree to mention it with a solemn nod whenever anyone says the word random.

title: The Day of the Stubborn Jar Lid
skyStory: The moon has wandered out of Aries and settled into Taurus, ninety-four percent lit and in no hurry whatsoever. Taurus moons love soft blankets, fresh bread and not being rushed. It is a moon with its feet up. Tomorrow it will be full, and it knows it, so tonight it is practising its glow in the mirror, very slowly, by candlelight.

reading: Something today will refuse to budge: a jar lid, a stuck drawer, a file that will not open, a decision that keeps sliding off the table. The Tiger will want to wrestle it. Taurus suggests running it under warm water and waiting.

That goes for people too. Someone will be stubborn about something small. Instead of pushing, ask them a question about it and listen to the whole answer. The lid comes off by itself around 6 pm, figuratively and maybe literally. The [[Knight of Pentacles]] rides slowly and always gets there. Today, so do you, a few minutes late and in excellent spirits.
joel.mission: Do one ordinary task today at exactly half your usual speed, and notice what you see that you normally miss.
joel.omen: A cow, a bull or a picture of one. Steady wins today; the universe has spoken in moos.

reading: Taurus is an earth sign, a cousin of yours, and it has brought you a basket of small comforts. A good pen. A warm sweater from the back of the closet. A window seat that is free when it is usually taken. Take all of it without explaining why you deserve it.

The Mountain is good at holding steady, but today it is allowed to be held. If someone offers to make you a cup of something, say yes before they finish the sentence. If a song comes on that you love, stop what you are doing for the whole of it. Saturn signs off on all of this personally.
nancy.mission: Find the coziest piece of clothing you own and wear it to at least one place it does not belong.
nancy.omen: A dog flopped completely flat on a warm floor. Total surrender is a form of wisdom today.

together.text: Share a list of five small luxuries each, the tiny things that make a day feel rich. A hot water bottle. A clean windshield. The first page of a new book. Compare lists. Steal one item from the other's list and make it happen for yourself tomorrow.

title: The Eve of the Recharge
skyStory: The moon is full tonight, ninety-eight percent lit and still lounging in Taurus like a pearl on a velvet cushion. It is the first full moon since this page woke up, and rumour says the first proper snowflakes of the season are queuing behind it. Tomorrow the moon will be at its absolute brightest. Tonight is the dress rehearsal, and it is already showing off.

reading: Full moons turn the volume up, and the Tiger is already loud. Today you will feel everything a little more: the good news, the small annoyances, the beauty of frost on a windshield. Notice which one gets most of your attention, then deliberately give the beautiful one twice as long.

Tonight is preparation. Find the bracelet, clean it gently with a soft cloth, and set it by the window where moonlight will reach it tomorrow. While you do, think of one thing you are ready to let go of. Not a big thing. A grudge against a printer counts. [[The Sun]] is warming up backstage and wants the room tidy.
joel.mission: Find the brightest window in the house and clear one small spot on its sill for tomorrow's ritual.
joel.omen: The first snowflake landing on your sleeve. Something new is starting, and it chose you specifically.
joel.stoneWhy: moon stone on the moon's eve

reading: The Wood Rat feels the full moon in its whiskers before anyone else does. You will be sharper today, quicker with a joke, faster to see the end of someone's sentence before they get there. Let them finish anyway. It is kinder, and you are usually right, which makes it twice as fun to wait.

Tonight, polish the ruby on your pinky and give it a little pep talk. Tomorrow it gets a full charge under the brightest moon of the season, and it should be ready. The mother of pearl wants in too. It is water, after all, and full moons pull on every tide, even the small one on your ring finger.
nancy.mission: Say goodnight to the moon out loud from a doorway, as if it is a neighbour you are fond of.
nancy.omen: A ring around the moon. Change is coming, and it is bringing good company with it.
nancy.stoneWhy: the tide stone, at high tide

together.text: Tomorrow is the Full Moon Recharge. Tonight, agree on a time to do it together, even miles apart. Pick it like a launch window: exact to the minute. Then both set an alarm with a ridiculous label, like Moon Laundry or Stone Spa Appointment.

title: The Great Full Moon Recharge
skyStory: One hundred percent. Every last inch of the moon is lit, and it has skipped into Gemini, the sign of the twins, which is frankly perfect for two people carrying each other's stones. Gemini loves a pair. Tonight it shines on the ruby and the onyx like a spotlight on a duet. Mars and Saturn have stopped bickering to watch. Even the gale holds its breath.

reading: Tonight is the Full Moon Recharge. Set the onyx bracelet on the windowsill where the moonlight lands, and leave it there while you do something slow by the fire. You will feel oddly light without it on your wrist, which is the point. Things that carry us need resting too.

While it charges, think about the [[Six of Pentacles]]: the giving hand and the receiving hand. Tonight the moon is the giver and you are only the one who holds still. Practise that. Let the light pour on something you love without doing anything about it. At bedtime, put the bracelet back on your left wrist, the receiving side, and feel it hum.
joel.mission: Charge the onyx under the moon for at least an hour, and do not check on it more than twice.
joel.omen: Moonlight making a bright square on the floor. That is your landing pad; stand in it for one breath.

reading: The ruby goes on the sill tonight, side by side with Joel's onyx in spirit, and probably in a photo too. Gemini doubles everything, so expect the moonlight to feel like it is shining on two windowsills at once, one by the cabin and one by the shore.

Bring all five stones if you like, a full council of elements lined up under the light: earth, fire, water, wind and heart, reporting for duty. Tell them the best story you have this month while they charge. They are an excellent audience. Then put the ruby back on your right pinky and admire it. It will look brighter. [[The Sun]] asks you to allow joy, and tonight it is shining right on your hand.
nancy.mission: Line up all five stones on the windowsill in element order and take one photo for Joel.
nancy.omen: A bright star sitting right beside the moon. Someone far away is shining back at you.

together.text: Recharge together at the agreed minute. Send one photo each of your stones in the moonlight, then switch: Joel moves the onyx to his right wrist for a minute to send strength, Nancy turns the ruby toward the window. Fire and Mountain, fully charged.

title: The Day of Two Conversations at Once
skyStory: Still full, ninety-eight percent, and the moon is chattering away in Gemini like it had three coffees after last night's party. Gemini moons talk with both hands and both sides of the mouth. Expect overlapping conversations, crossed messages and somebody calling you by the wrong name with total confidence. It is all affectionate. The twins are just very, very excited.

reading: Two conversations will happen at once today, and you will try to win both. Gemini thinks this is hilarious. Life Path 3 can absolutely talk to two people, but listening to two people is a separate skill, and today the sky is grading listening.

Around 12:30 someone will tell a story that goes on too long. Do not jump in with your own better story, even though yours has a plot twist and a sound effect. Ask them one question about theirs instead. Their face will light up like the moon last night. Save your story for Nancy later; she will appreciate the twist.
joel.mission: Ask three people today a question you have never asked them before, and remember all three answers.
joel.omen: Two identical cars parked nose to nose. A conversation is about to become a duet; harmonise.

reading: Gemini is the storyteller's moon and your hands have been waiting all week for this. Today someone will ask, almost casually, 'so what happened?' and you will get to tell the whole thing, with voices, pauses and a dramatic reveal.

The Rat's trick: tell it twice. Once to someone who already knows the ending, so you can enjoy their laugh at your favourite part. Once to someone brand new, so you can watch the surprise land. Two audiences, one story, full Gemini energy. The [[Page of Cups]] has a fish popping out of its cup and is just as surprised as everyone else.
nancy.mission: Tell your best story of the week to two different people, and change one tiny detail the second time.
nancy.omen: A crow or any bird that seems to be talking back. Someone wants to hear more from you.

together.text: Have a conversation entirely in questions. Every message must be a question. First one to accidentally write a statement loses and must send a dramatic apology in the style of a medieval herald. Gemini is refereeing and has no mercy.

title: The Day the Cabin Hogged the Blankets
skyStory: The moon has slipped into Cancer, its own home sign, ninety-four percent lit and very happy to be back. Cancer moons nest. They pile up quilts, light the lamps early and insist everyone take their shoes off. Outside, the late November dark arrives before supper. Inside, every hearth glows a little brighter, as if the moon whispered a reminder to all of them at once.

reading: The cabin is in full nesting mode today. Every blanket in the place has migrated to one couch and the woodstove is crackling like it is telling stories. The Tiger may grumble about too much coziness. It will lose.

Home is the assignment. Fix one small thing that has bugged you for months: the squeaky hinge, the drawer that sticks, the lamp that flickers. Then sit near the thing you fixed and admire it unreasonably. Someone will come by or call, and the right move is to let them make you the warm drink. The [[Ten of Cups]] is drawing a rainbow over the roofline and would like you to look up.
joel.mission: Oil one squeaky hinge, or fix one tiny thing, and give it a small round of applause.
joel.omen: Smoke rising straight up from a chimney on a still evening. All is well at home base.

reading: The tide comes up to the edge of the woods today and stops politely, like a guest wiping its feet. Cancer is a water sign and it wants you to feel at home in yourself, not just in your house.

Make one corner of your space a little more yours. A photo on the wall. A shell on the sill. A candle that smells like the forest after rain. When you sit there tonight, tell the room a story about where that object came from. The room has been waiting for a good storyteller. Everything else can wait until morning, and it will, grumbling quietly in the hallway.
nancy.mission: Put one small object you love somewhere you will see it first thing tomorrow morning.
nancy.omen: A crab, a shell or a picture of the sea in an unexpected place. Home is following you around.

together.text: Each of you send a photo of the coziest corner you have right now. No staging allowed, real clutter and all. Rate each other's corner out of eleven, with one bonus point for a blanket and two for a sleeping animal.

title: The Day of the Returned Casserole Dish
skyStory: Eighty-seven percent and beginning, ever so gently, to wane, the moon is still tucked up in Cancer, where it is writing thank-you notes. Cancer remembers every kindness ever done for it, in order, with dates. Tonight it wants things returned to where they belong: borrowed books, odd mittens, warm feelings that went unspoken. It has a list. It is a long list.

reading: Somewhere in your life is a borrowed thing that needs to go home: a dish, a book, a tool, a charger. It has been politely waiting. Today the moon would like it returned, with a tiny note attached that says something kind.

Here is the plot twist: when you return it, they will try to give you something back. A jar of jam, a compliment, a story. The [[Six of Pentacles]] is watching closely. Do not say 'oh, you shouldn't have'. Say 'thank you, I love it' and carry it home like a trophy. Receiving is a sport, and today you are in the league.
joel.mission: Return one borrowed thing today with a three-word note tucked inside it.
joel.omen: A neighbour waving from across the road. A small circle of kindness is about to close.

reading: The Rat keeps a mental list of every favour, every kindness, every time someone lent a hand. Today the moon asks you to read one entry out loud. Find someone who helped you level up this year and tell them, specifically, what difference it made.

Do it in your own storyteller style. Not 'thanks for everything', but 'remember that afternoon in March when you showed me how to do the thing, and I have used it ninety times since'. Specific gratitude is a gift that keeps glowing. Watch their face. That is the best story you will hear all day.
nancy.mission: Send one thank-you message today that includes a specific date, place or detail.
nancy.omen: A kettle coming to the boil the moment someone walks into the room. Good timing is on your side.
nancy.stoneWhy: the bracelet on your left wrist

together.text: Share a gratitude feast: each of you list five tiny things you are thankful for from the past month, the more oddly specific the better. A perfect parking spot counts. A dog that sneezed at you counts. Read them aloud to each other if you can.

title: The Day of the Golden Scarf
skyStory: The moon has strutted into Leo, seventy-eight percent lit and wearing sunglasses at night. Leo moons crave applause. They want a stage, a spotlight and somebody to say bravo at the right moment. Leo is also ruled by the Sun, so tonight the moon is borrowing a golden glow and pretending it was always hers. Nobody is brave enough to correct her.

reading: Around 10:15 this morning a stranger in a mustard-gold scarf will hold a door for you and say 'after you' with a theatrical little bow. You will laugh, because who bows anymore? Leo moons, that is who.

Later, Nancy will message you about her day. A stranger. A gold scarf. A theatrical bow. The same two words. Don't even scream, but definitely scream a little. Two strangers, two towns, one scarf colour. The universe has clearly hired a costume department. Accept the door, accept the bow, and accept the [[Three of Cups]] energy: somewhere, someone is celebrating you.
joel.mission: Hold a door for someone today with an unnecessary flourish, and do it with a perfectly straight face.
joel.omen: Something gold glinting on the ground. A small gift is on its way, probably in the form of an excellent compliment.

reading: Leo is a fire sign and today it is lending you a little stage presence. People will turn when you walk in. Somebody will laugh at your joke before you get to the punchline. A stranger in a gold scarf will hold a door and bow.

When you tell Joel about the scarf and he sends back his own gold-scarf stranger, bow and all, give it the full ΔΕΣ treatment: hands up, eyes wide, maybe a spin in the kitchen. Then accept the spotlight. [[Strength]] is a lion at peace, and it says you are allowed to be adored without earning it first.
nancy.mission: Accept the next compliment you get with a small curtsy or bow, in full view of everyone.
nancy.omen: A cat sitting in a sunbeam like royalty. You, too, are allowed to take the warm spot.

together.text: Write a short review of each other as if the other were a stage show. Five stars, one dramatic quote, one standing-ovation moment. Joel reviews Nancy, Nancy reviews Joel. Read them out loud, gold scarf optional but strongly recommended.

title: The Day of the Grand Exit
skyStory: Last quarter, sixty-seven percent lit, and the moon is taking its final bows in Leo. Last quarter is the moon's clearing-out phase: it sheds a little light every night like a performer removing glitter after a show. Leo insists on one more curtain call anyway. The audience, mostly seagulls and a fox, applauds politely. Tomorrow it will be backstage, tidying.

reading: The Tiger has been carrying something for weeks that it no longer needs: an old plan, a project that fizzled, a should that belongs to someone else. Today you can set it down, take a bow and walk off stage left. No farewell speech necessary. The [[Eight of Swords]] was only ever a cage made of thoughts.

Make a tiny ceremony of it. Write the thing on a scrap of paper, fold it twice and drop it in the woodstove or the recycling, whichever feels more theatrical. Then do one thing that makes you feel light: a walk at dusk, a song turned up loud, a long look at the stars. Notice how much more room there is in the cabin.
joel.mission: Recycle or give away three things today, and narrate each farewell like a sports commentator.
joel.omen: A leaf letting go of a branch in still air. Letting go can be graceful, quiet and entirely voluntary.
joel.elementWhy: burn off what you no longer need

reading: The Wood Rat is a collector by nature, and somewhere in the nest is a pile of things kept just in case. Today one of those things gets to leave. You will know which one: it will feel lighter the moment you decide. The nest will feel roomier by bedtime.

Last quarter moons love a clear-out, and Leo wants it done with flair. Hold the object up, tell it one story about why you kept it, thank it and let it go. The hollow wish of the [[Nine of Cups]] loosens its grip a little every time you choose what you actually want over what you thought you should want.
nancy.mission: Choose one thing kept just in case and give it a proper send-off speech before it leaves.
nancy.omen: An empty shelf catching the afternoon light. Space is a gift, and you just gave it to yourself.

together.text: Each of you name one thing you are leaving behind in November. Say it once, out loud or in a message, then never mention it again this year. Replace it with one word you want to carry into December. Nancy's birthday month is coming, and it deserves a clean stage.

title: The Day of the Labelled Drawer
skyStory: The moon has moved into Virgo, fifty-seven percent lit and carrying a label maker. Virgo moons sort, tidy and alphabetise; they find crumbs in corners nobody knew existed. It is the last day of November, the dark is long and the first real snow is gossiping at the edge of the forecast. Virgo would like everything in its proper drawer before December walks in.

reading: One drawer in the cabin has become a legend: odd keys, old batteries, three mystery cables, a single chess piece. Today Virgo hands you a label maker, metaphorically, and asks you to sort it. Ten minutes. Not a whole room. One drawer.

As you sort, you will find something you thought was gone forever, probably small, probably silly, definitely delightful. Keep it on the desk as a trophy. The month started with one spark, one plan and a brand-new moon. It ends with an orderly drawer and a full heart. The [[Knight of Wands]] salutes you with a slightly smaller torch, which is progress.
joel.mission: Sort one drawer in ten minutes flat, timer on, and label it with a ridiculous official name.
joel.omen: A lost key turning up exactly where you already looked. Something you gave up on is ready to come back.

reading: December is knocking, and December is your month: the solstice, the light returning, your birthday glowing on the horizon like a lighthouse. Virgo sees it coming and wants to help you get the shore ready. Expect the tide to tidy the beach overnight, all by itself.

Make a short list, in your best handwriting, of three things you want to do for yourself before the solstice. Not for anyone else. Not to earn anything. Just three joys, written down where Saturn can see them. [[The Sun]] is warming up on the far side of the long dark, and it has already started counting down.
nancy.mission: Write three solstice wishes for yourself on a card and tuck it behind the mirror until December 22.
nancy.omen: Neatly stacked firewood or a perfectly folded towel. Order is a love letter, and someone is writing you one.
nancy.stoneWhy: your left wrist, steady and sure
nancy.elementWhy: solid ground for the turning year

together.text: Look back at the word you each picked on the tenth. Did November live up to it? Score it out of eleven. Then choose a word for December together, one word, shared, and write it somewhere you will both see it every day until the solstice.
